newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian tin firm to raise share capital.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian tin firm to raise share capital.

text.p: The Nigerian Tin and Allied Minerals Products Ltd, which produces the bulk of the country's tin output, said on Wednesday it would increase its share capital to 500 million naira from 500,000 naira currently.

The News agency of Nigeria reported that the company's chief executive, Gallio Dagu, said in its base in Jos, central Nigeria that this was to prepare the firm for the challenges of modern mining as well as demands from the international tin market.

"If high capacity equipment can be provided, a minimum 40 tonnes of what is currently produced for the month can also be exported to earn foreign exchange," Dagu told officials of the ministry of solid minerals during a visit to its premises.
Nigeria, which heads the Association of Tin Producing Countries (ATPC), has an annual export level of 1,800 tonnes and produces about 2,500 tonnes yearly.
The solid minerals ministry was established last year as part of a plan to encourage the development of solid minerals which Nigeria says it has in abundance.
Nigeria used to produce about 10,000 tonnes of tin metals in the 1950s but gradually allowed mines to wither away as it found crude oil which brought in billions of dollars.
Dagu said the company could acquire a small capacity smelting furnace to add value to its exported tin.
He said the company had received proposals from Britain and Malaysia requiring monthly supply of at least 40 tonnes and 100 tonnes of tin, respectively.
"The export market for tin is guaranteed and inexhaustible," he said.
